title: Three equations for steady acceleration
text:
Read and explain

Target R5

Three equations for steady acceleration

EquationUseful when…

v = v₀ + atYou need velocity or time

Δx = v₀t + ½at²You know the time taken

v² = v₀² + 2aΔxTime is not given or needed

All three work when acceleration stays the same. **Choose the positive direction before** you add signs.

title: Negative acceleration, positive displacement
text:
**2026**-XJ · No Clock · Graphic novel, page **30**

Negative acceleration, positive displacement

The novel has its own practice car. It starts at positive thirty meters each second. Its acceleration stays at negative six meters per second squared. It moves positive seventy-five meters while braking. Nadia says it moves forward as it slows. This answer leaves out the distance before braking starts.

The novel uses **+30 m/s** and **−6 m/s²**. The slide before this uses **+20 m/s** and **−4 m/s²**. Both objects stop.

Why are both displacements positive? **Check each** with time and average velocity.

Part **2** · Check the result another way · Write your own answer in Work.

title: Check displacement with average velocity
text:
I do · displacement

Target R5 Pairs

An average can make the math easier

If acceleration stays the same, average the start and end velocities.

(**0** + **4**) ÷ **2** = **2 m/s**

Displacement: **2** × **4** = **8 m**

Same area: triangle or average

Same area: triangle or average. Velocity (m/s) versus Time (s). The shortcut requires constant acceleration.

This shortcut works when acceleration stays the same.

title: At the top, which quantity is zero?
text:
**2026**-XJ · No Clock · Graphic novel, page **31**

At the top, which quantity is zero?

This paper model leaves out air resistance. Up is positive. Launch velocity is fifteen meters each second. Final upward velocity is zero. Acceleration is negative 9.8 meters per second squared. The rise is about 11.5 meters.

The novel’s paper example starts at **15 m/s**. This slide uses **14 m/s**. Gravity acts at the top in both cases.

Why is velocity zero at the top, but acceleration is not? **Explain why the balls rise** different amounts.
